Use the REST API to render a Markdown document as an HTML page or as raw text. This endpoint accepts a JSON body describing the text to render and how to render it. Request curl -L \ -X POST \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-TOKEN>" \ -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \ https://api.github.com/markdown \ -d '{"text":"Hello **world**"}'
Body parameters 1 Name T ype Required Description text string Y es The Markdown text to render in HTML. mode string No The rendering mode. Default: markdown.

Can be one of: mark down, gfm. context string No The repository context to use when creating references in gfm mode. Response "

Hello world

" Notes In raw mode, GitHub Flavored Markdown is not supported and Markdown is rendered in plain format, similar to a README.md file. Markdown content must be 400 KB or less. 2

Render a Markdown document Applies to API version 2025-06-01 and later. Renders a Markdown document server-side, returning either an HTML fragment or raw text depending on the requested mode. T wo changes from earlier API versions: the context field now accepts an owner/repo pair as a structured object rather than a plain string, and a new wrap_tables flag controls whether wide tables are wrapped for narrow viewports. curl -L \ -X POST \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \

curl -L \ -X POST \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-TOKEN>" \ -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2025-06-01" \ https://api.github.com/markdown \ -d '{"text":"Hello **world**","wrap_tables":true}' Parameters accepted in the request body:
text (string, required) — The Markdown text to render.
mode (string, optional, default markdown) — One of markdown or gfm.
context (object, optional) — { ”owner”: ”...”, ”repo”: ”...” }. Used for gfm-mode reference linking.

wrap_tables (boolean, optional, default false) — When true, wide tables render with hori- zontal scroll wrappers instead of overflowing. Response body is an HTML string (or raw text, in raw mode). Content must be 400 KB or less.

Previous version (2022-11-28) The prior version of this endpoint accepted only text, mode, and context, where context was a plain string (e.g. ”octocat/Hello-World”) rather than a structured object. There was no wrap_ta bles option in that version — wide tables in rendered output simply overflowed their container with no wrapping behavior available. 3
Create an issue POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues Any user with pull access to a repository can create an issue. Parameters

Name In T ype Description owner path string Required. The account owner of the repository . repo path string Required. The name of the repository without the .git extension. title body string or integer Required. The title of the issue. body body string The contents of the issue. assignee body string Login for the user that this issue should be assigned to. labels body array of strings Labels to associate with this issue.
Example request curl -L \ -X POST \ -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \ https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/issues \ -d '{"title":"Found a bug","body":"I'\''m having a problem."}'
Example response { "id": 1, "number": 1347, "state": "open", "title": "Found a bug" } 4

Create an issue POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues API version 2025-06-01 Creates an issue on the specified repository . Any user with pull access can create one. Starting in this version, assignee is deprecated in favor of assignees (array), and a new optional type field lets you set the issue type at creation time instead of via a separate call.
Path parameters Name T ype Description owner string The account owner of the repository . repo string The name of the repository .

Body parameters Name T ype Required Default Description title string or integer Y es — The title of the issue. body string No null The contents of the issue. assignees array of strings No [] Logins for the users assigned to this issue.
section: Name T ype Required Default Description

content: Replaces the deprecated assi gnee field. labels array of strings No [] Labels to associate with this issue. type string No null The name of the issue type to set on creation. curl -L -X POST \ -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2025-06-01" \ https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/issues \ -d '{"title":"Found a bug","assignees":["octocat"],"type":"Bug"}'

Previous version (2022-11-28) The prior version of this endpoint only accepted a single assignee (string) rather than an as signees array, so an issue could only be assigned to one user at creation time — assigning multiple users required a separate follow-up call. There was also no type field; setting an issue type required a second request after creation. 5

Create a pull request Draft pull requests are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Pro, GitHub T eam and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For more information, see the GitHub products page. T o create a pull request you provide a title, base and head branches, and optionally a body describing the change.
Endpoint: POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls Parameters:
title — string — required — The title of the new pull request.
head — string — required — The name of the branch where your changes are imple- mented.
base — string — required — The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into.
body — string — optional — The contents of the pull request.

draft — boolean — optional, default false — Indicates whether the pull request is a draft. curl -X POST https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/pulls \ -d '{"title":"Amazing feature","head":"octocat:new-feature","base":"master"}' Returns a pull request object on success (status 201). 6

Create a pull request Version 2025-06-01 · reference Overview Opens a pull request against the given repository . Since 2025-06-01, the API supports speci- fying maintainer_can_modify at creation time (previously this required a follow-up PATCH call), and draft pull requests can be created directly as ready-for-review by omitting the field entirely — its default has not changed but its interaction with auto-merge settings has.

Path parameters Name T ype owner string repo string Request body Field T ype Required Notes title string Y es Required unless issue is specified. head string Y es Branch or user:branc h for cross-repo. base string Y es The branch you want changes merged into. body string No PR description. draft boolean No Default false. maintainer_can_modi fy boolean No Default true. Now settable at creation time. Example curl -X POST -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2025-06-01" \ https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/pulls \

https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/pulls \ -d '{"title":"Amazing feature", "head":"octocat:new-feature", "base":"master", "maintainer_can_modify":false}' Returns 201 Created with the pull request object.

Previous version (2022-11-28) maintainer_can_modify could not be set at creation time in the prior version — it was true by default with no way to override it until a follow-up PATCH request. The interaction between d raft and auto-merge settings also behaved differently: a draft PR could not have auto-merge enabled until explicitly marked ready for review, whereas this version allows auto-merge to be pre-armed on a draft. 7
Create a repository for the authenticated user POST /user/repos Creates a new repository for the authenticated user. OAuth scope required: public_repo or repo scope.

Parameter T ype Required Description name string yes The name of the repository . description string no A short description of the repository . homepage string no A URL with more information about the repository . private boolean no Whether the repository is private. Default: false. has_issues boolean no Whether issues are enabled. Default: tru e. auto_init boolean no Pass true to create an initial commit with empty README. Default: false. curl -X POST https://api.github.com/user/repos \
Default: false. curl -X POST https://api.github.com/user/repos \ -d '{"name":"Hello-World","private":true}' 8

Create a repository for the authenticated user POST /user/repos — API version 2025-06-01 What changed As of this version, has_issues defaults to true only for public repositories; private repositories now default has_issues to false unless explicitly set. A new visibility enum field supersedes the boolean private for organizations offering internal repositories, though private continues to work for personal accounts. Parameters
name (string, required) — Repository name.
description (string, optional) — Short repository description.
visibility (enum, optional) — One of public, private, internal. Default: public.
private (boolean, optional, deprecated in favor of visibility) — Default: false.
has_issues (boolean, optional) — Default depends on visibility: true for public, false for private/internal.

auto_init (boolean, optional) — Default: false. Creates an initial commit with an empty README when true. Request curl -X POST -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2025-06-01" \ https://api.github.com/user/repos \ -d '{"name":"Hello-World","visibility":"internal","auto_init":true}' Response Returns 201 Created with the full repository object.

Previous version (2022-11-28) The prior version only had the boolean private field — there was no visibility enum, and orga- nizations offering “internal” visibility had no way to request it through this endpoint. has_iss ues also defaulted to true unconditionally, regardless of whether the repository was public or private. 9

Create a release Users with push access to the repository can create a release. This endpoint triggers notifications. Creating content too quickly using this endpoint may result in secondary rate limiting.
Parameters for “Create a release” Path parameters Name T ype Description owner string The account owner of the repository . repo string The name of the repository .

Body parameters A release requires a git tag to point to. If the tag already exists, this endpoint attaches the release to that tag; otherwise a lightweight tag with that name is created automatically at the target commitish when the release is published, and this automatic behavior is one of the more commonly misunderstood parts of the release flow because many integrators assume they must create the tag themselves beforehand via the Git Data API, when in fact simply

they must create the tag themselves beforehand via the Git Data API, when in fact simply supplying tag_name against a target_commitish that does not yet carry that tag is sufficient and is in fact the more common pattern seen across the majority of CI/CD release pipelines that call this endpoint directly after a successful build, since it saves a full extra round trip through the separate tags endpoint and reduces the chance of a race condition between tag creation and release creation.

Name T ype Required Description tag_name string Y es The name of the tag. target_commitish string No Specifies the commitish value that determines where the Git tag is created from. Default: the repository’s default branch. name string No The name of the release. body string No T ext describing the contents of the tag. draft boolean No true makes the release a draft. Default: false. prerelease boolean No true identifies the release as a prerelease. Default: f alse. 10

Name T ype Required Description generate_release_not es boolean No Whether to automatically generate the name and body for this release. Default: fals e. curl -L -X POST https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/releases \ -d '{"tag_name":"v1.0.0", "target_commitish":"master", "name":"v1.0.0", "draft":false, "prerelease":false}' Returns 201 Created with the release object. 11

Create a release API version 2025-06-01 Summary Publishes a new release against an existing or new tag. As of this version, discussion_categ ory_name can be supplied to automatically open a linked discussion, and make_latest gives explicit control over whether the release becomes the repository’s “Latest” release, replacing an older undocumented heuristic based purely on publish date.

Body parameters Name T ype Required Default Description tag_name string Y es — The name of the tag. target_commitis h string No default branch Commitish value the tag is created from, if it doesn’t already exist. name string No null Release title. body string No null Release notes body text. draft boolean No false Creates a draft (unpublished) release when tru e. prerelease boolean No false Marks the release as a prerelease. discussion_cate gory_name string No null If specified, a discussion of the specified category is created and
section: Name T ype Required Default Description

content: discussion of the specified category is created and linked to the release. generate_releas e_notes boolean No false Auto-generates name/body from merged PRs since the previous release. make_latest enum No true One of true, fals e, legacy . Controls whether this release is marked “Latest”. 12 Example curl -L -X POST -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2025-06-01" \ https://api.github.com/repos/octocat/Hello-World/releases \ -d '{"tag_name":"v2.0.0","make_latest":"true","generate_release_notes":true}' Returns 201 Created.
section: Name T ype Required Default Description

content: Previous version (2022-11-28) The prior version had no discussion_category_name field, so linking a discussion to a release required a separate manual step in the UI after the release was published. There was also no make_latest control — whether a release showed as “Latest” was determined purely by an internal heuristic based on publish date and prerelease/draft status, which occasionally marked an older release as “Latest” if a newer one was still in draft. 13
